Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is a gerbe over <MATH_0003>, and
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0004> and
<MATH_0005>
are surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.
<STRUCT_0004>

The implication (1) <MATH_0001> (2) follows from
Lemmas <REF_0001> and <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (2). It suffices to prove (1) for the base change of <MATH_0002>
by a surjective, flat, and locally finitely presented morphism
<MATH_0003>, see
Lemma <REF_0003> (note that the base change
of the diagonal of <MATH_0004> is the diagonal of the base change). 
Thus we may assume <MATH_0005> is a scheme <MATH_0006>.
In this case <MATH_0007>
is a base change of <MATH_0008> and
we conclude that <MATH_0009> is a gerbe
by Proposition <REF_0004>.
We still have to show that <MATH_0010> is a gerbe over <MATH_0011>.
Let <MATH_0012> be the morphism of
Lemma <REF_0005>
turning <MATH_0013> into a gerbe over the algebraic space <MATH_0014>
classifying isomorphism classes of objects of <MATH_0015>.
It is clear that <MATH_0016> factors as
<MATH_0017>. Since <MATH_0018> is surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation, we conclude that <MATH_0019> is
surjective as a map of fppf sheaves (for example use
Lemma <REF_0006>).
On the other hand, <MATH_0020> is injective too: for any scheme
<MATH_0021> and any two <MATH_0022>-valued points <MATH_0023> of <MATH_0024> which map to
the same point of <MATH_0025>, we can first fppf locally on <MATH_0026>
lift <MATH_0027> to objects <MATH_0028> of <MATH_0029> over <MATH_0030>
and second deduce that <MATH_0031> and <MATH_0032> are fppf locally isomorphic
by our assumption that
<MATH_0033>
is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.
Whence <MATH_0034> by construction of <MATH_0035>.
Thus <MATH_0036> and the proof is complete.
